purpose: A portable request/response contract for handing any product design to clinozy-fe's theming system. Send `request` to the design source; it returns `response`; clinozy-fe applies it. Works for any project, not just this one — the enums below are clinozy-fe's vocabulary, so swapping the `vocabulary` block retargets the contract at a different design system.
status: PROPOSED — no importer exists yet. See `gaps` at the bottom.

axes.what: The design is expressed purely as selections from clinozy-fe's 18 orthogonal design axes, plus one seed hue.
axes.cost: Zero CSS. No new files. Applied at runtime by the existing generated-look engine (`customTheme`).
axes.useWhen: Most cases. The design is a coherent look/feel rather than a locked corporate palette.
axes.limitation: You get a generated palette derived from the seed hue and harmony rule — not exact brand hexes.

tokens.what: Explicit OKLCH values per semantic token, light + dark.
tokens.cost: One hand-authored CSS block plus registration in 4 files (see `applyTo.tokens`).
tokens.useWhen: A brand mandates exact colors (e.g. Anthropic terracotta #c96442) that a generated palette cannot reproduce.
tokens.limitation: Every value must pass the AA gate; brand hexes often need a darkened text variant (see `constraints.contrast`).

twoDeliveryModes.recommendation: Ask for BOTH. `axes` gives an instant preview with no code; `tokens` is the exact-brand fallback. They are not exclusive — a token preset can also declare axis defaults.

instructionsForDesignSource: Return ONE JSON object matching `response.schema` below. No prose outside it.
Every axis value MUST come from `vocabulary` — these are enums, not free text. An unlisted value is rejected by the consumer.
All colors MUST be OKLCH: `oklch(L C H)` with L in 0..1, C in 0..0.4, H in 0..360. No hex, rgb, or hsl in token values.
Provide BOTH `light` and `dark`. A design that only works in one mode is incomplete — clinozy-fe ships a mode toggle.

Every foreground/background text pair MUST meet WCAG AA 4.5:1. State the computed ratio for each in `accessibility.verifiedPairs`. If a brand color fails, keep it for non-text tokens (ring, chart) and darken/lighten the text variant — do not silently ship a failing pair.
Do not invent token names. Use only the names in `vocabulary.semanticTokens`.
If you cannot satisfy a constraint, say so explicitly in `notes` rather than approximating.

brand.name: string — product/company name
brand.primaryHex: string|null — the mandated brand color, if any
brand.logoDescription: string|null — informs neutral temperature and accent intensity

product.domain: string — e.g. 'B2B analytics dashboard', 'consumer social', 'clinical records'
product.audience: string — who uses it, in what setting

constraintsFromConsumer.note: Send this block verbatim — it is what makes the output actually installable.
constraintsFromConsumer.semanticTokensOnly: Raw palette values may appear ONLY in token definitions, never as utility classes. Consumer enforces via `pnpm validate:tokens`.
constraintsFromConsumer.contrastFloor: WCAG 2.1 AA — 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI boundaries
constraintsFromConsumer.mustNotOverride: Font files, icon set, or component library — the consumer owns those. Reference them by axis id only.

vocabulary._note: clinozy-fe's real catalogs, read from src/shared/theme/presets.ts. Replace this block to retarget another design system.

accentColor.drives: seed hue for the generated palette

harmony.drives: how chart/secondary hues derive from the accent

preset.id: string — kebab-case, unique, becomes the [data-theme='<id>'] selector
preset.label: string — human label for the Appearance picker
preset.rationale: string — 1-3 sentences on why this look fits the product

axes._comment: Delivery mode 1. Every key optional; omitted keys inherit the default from `vocabulary`.

tokens._comment: Delivery mode 2. Omit entirely for an axes-only design.

nonTextExemptions.<token-name>: reason it is exempt from 4.5:1 (decorative, non-text)

schema.notes: string — anything the consumer must know: unmet constraints, brand compromises, deliberate omissions.

preset.label: Claude
preset.rationale: Warm terracotta accent on a neutral base — reads as considered and editorial without competing with dense content.

nonTextExemptions.--color-ring: Focus ring — true brand #c96442 kept here; 3.74:1 is below the text floor but ring is non-text.

minimalExample.notes: Brand hex #c96442 fails AA for text at 3.74:1. Kept verbatim for ring and chart-1; text surfaces use a darkened L=0.55 variant.

steps: Map each axis value onto the customTheme state in useThemeStore.
src/index.css — add [data-theme='<id>'] and .dark[data-theme='<id>'] blocks from response.tokens.
src/index.css — add .theme-dot-<id> { background-color: <accent> } for the picker swatch.
src/shared/theme/presets.ts — add { id, label } to THEME_PRESETS.
public/theme-init.js — add <id> to PRESET_PRIMARY (light/dark [primary, primaryForeground]). Skipping this causes a flash of the default accent on every cold load.
Optional: set DEFAULT_PRESET = '<id>' to ship it out of the box.

gaps.noImporter: Nothing in clinozy-fe reads this JSON. Applying a response is currently manual (the 4 steps above). A `pnpm theme:import <file.json>` script would close this — it would need to write the CSS block, patch the two registries, and run the validators.
gaps.noSchemaValidation: There is no JSON Schema file enforcing this shape at runtime. The `response.schema` block above is descriptive, not executable.
gaps.axesNotRoundTripped: The generated-look axes are settable in the UI but there is no export path that emits this JSON from a live theme, so design↔code sync is one-way today.
gaps.contrastNotAutomated: AA ratios are verified by hand (OKLCH→sRGB→WCAG). Worth a test that fails the build on a sub-4.5:1 text pair in any registered preset.
